# dsh-adhd-mode
ADHD-friendly output style for DeepSeek Harness. It puts a ruleset in the system prompt that makes r
eplies easier to act on: the next action first, numbered steps, state restated each turn, no preambl
e. You can switch it on and off while a session is running.
A port of ayghri/i-have-adhd (MIT). The ruleset in `skills/adhd-mode/rules.md` is upstream's text wi
th one paragraph replaced: upstream is turned off when the reader says a phrase, and this bundle has
no phrase to say (what changed).
中文说明
## What this replaces
Upstream is a set of glue scripts, one per runtime. On Claude Code it registers a `SessionStart` hoo
k that pastes the ruleset into the session, and keeps an "always on" flag file at `~/.claude/.i-have
-adhd-always`. DSH has no session-start hook, so all three pieces live in one bundle here:
| Piece | Upstream | Here |
| hook | `SessionStart` hook | an `agent.ctx`-scoped `systemPrompt.section()` with a dynamic `text`

|
| switch | flag file under `~/.claude/` | a `.volatile()` config field, live and persisted |
| pag
e | none | a settings page and an icon+label trigger in the composer tool row |
## Changes from upstream
One paragraph of the ruleset is not upstream's: `## Persistence`. Upstream turns the mode off when t
he reader says "stop adhd mode", and its `SessionStart` hook re-pastes the ruleset whenever a sessio
n starts, resumes or compacts. Neither can happen here — the Host half matches no text — so that par
agraph now says the switch lives outside the conversation and that nothing said in the conversation
changes the mode. Everything else in `skills/adhd-mode/rules.md` is upstream's text, frontmatter inc
luded; the `disable-model-invocation` flag is inert because this bundle never registers the file as
he `disable-model-invocation` flag is inert because this bundle never registers the file as a skill.
Upstream's ruleset moves slowly (the project is mostly per-runtime glue), so there is no sync workfl
ow: this copy is a fork, edited by hand.
## Install

That is the whole install. `dsh plugin` forwards the rest of the line to pnpm inside the profile, an
d the next boot promotes any new dependency that declares `dsh.bundle` to a profile layer on its own
— there is no second step. Restart the profile afterwards.

Installing from a working tree you intend to edit takes one extra step: see live-edit install.
## Use
Two places, both in the Web UI:
| Where | What |

| the `ADHD` button in the composer tool row | click to flip |
| Settings → ADHD output mode | the s

in the composer tool row | click to flip |
| Settings → ADHD output mode | the switch on the page |
The change lands on the next model step and is written to the profile's config, so it survives a res
tart. There is no command, no tool and nothing to type — the UI is the only control, and the only pl
ace to look when the mode is not doing what you expected.
The switch is profile-wide, not per session. DSH's `PromptSection` takes no session key, so there is
nowhere to store whether the mode was on in one particular session.
What *is* scoped is the injection. The section is registered on the agent's own context rather than
the plugin's, so the ruleset reaches the agent the reader is talking to and stops there. A delegated
child — anything spawned with a delegation depth, which includes Agent Teams teammates — joins its
parent's preset and assembles with its own persona and tool set, never with this section. A session
forked from another is a top-level agent the reader opened on purpose, so it does get the section.
## Config
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `false` | volatile; the switch the UI writes |
| `order` | `15` | position of the sect
ion in the system prompt |

## Versions
Semantic versioning. The compatibility surface is small — the loader row id and the settings namespa
ce, the two strings a profile stores — so the rules are about what an existing install would have to
the two strings a profile stores — so the rules are about what an existing install would have to do:
| Bump | When |
| MAJOR | an install has to be redone: the loader row id or the settings namespace changes, a config

field disappears, or the bundle needs a newer DSH |
| MINOR | the reader gets something new, or the

injection changes: a new seat, a new config field, a new language, a different prompt section |
| P
ATCH | a fix nobody has to react to: ruleset wording, docs, tests, internal refactors |
`package.json` holds the version, `CHANGELOG.md` records what is in it, and `[Unreleased]` accumulat
es until it is frozen. Cutting a release is one command:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That bumps the version, turns the `[Unreleased]` entries into a dated section, runs the tests, commi
ts, and pushes the tag. `.github/workflows/release.yml` then publishes the GitHub release from that
section. CI refuses a tag that disagrees with `package.json`, and a `doctor` job refuses a version t
hat no changelog section explains.
The plugin market reads the version out of `package.json`, so the number here is what a listing show
s. This project is not published to npm, so nothing depends on the number for resolution — but the t
ag is the only immutable pointer to "the code a reader had".
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`test/host.mjs` loads `index.js` against a fake Cordis context and checks that exactly one section r
egisters per top-level agent, that a delegated child gets none while a fork still gets one, that the
ruleset appears only while the switch is on, and that the Host half exposes no command, tool or phr
ase matching. `test/client.mjs` loads `client.js` against stub browser globals and a stub React, the
n renders both seats in `zh` and `en`.
Neither test needs DSH, a browser, or `npm install`.
